public_rationale: ARC Prize's December 20, 2024 report recorded an 87.5% score for a high-compute o3 preview configuration, while also reporting failures on some very easy tasks [e1, e2]. Government pre-deployment testing in 2024 found tool-calling and output-formatting problems in the tested o1 version [e3]. The GPT-4 preprint revised on April 13, 2023 reported broad capabilities and argued for an early, incomplete form of AGI [e4]. These findings document both capabilities and limitations, but do not establish or exclude an adequate empirical basis for human-comparable flexibility, resourcefulness and reliability across representative tasks as of January 7, 2025 [e1, e2, e3, e4].
limitations: The evaluations do not comprehensively cover systems existing on January 7, 2025 or provide a shared threshold for Marcus's definition.
The cited ARC results concern the December 2024 research preview, not the later released o3.
The government findings apply only to the tested pre-deployment o1 version; reported results include assistance from adapted agent designs.
The GPT-4 researchers' description of incomplete AGI does not establish Marcus's reliability standard.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There is zero justification for claiming that current technology has achieved general intelligence.

statement.excerpt: But there is zero justification for claiming that the current technology has achieved general intelligence.
statement.document_title: The Five Stages of AGI Grief

from_speaker: flexible and general, with resourcefulness and reliability comparable to (or beyond) human intelligence
our_interpretation: Read the claim as saying there was no adequate empirical basis for declaring general intelligence achieved under Marcus's accompanying definition. Evidence of individual general abilities would not by itself contradict this reading.

The target is the state of technology on the publication date, 2025-01-07. Capability evaluations have no regular reporting period, so use that snapshot rather than inventing a reporting quarter. Earlier evaluations provide context.
Include demonstrated research systems existing by publication, even if they were not generally available.
Human-comparable reliability does not require perfection. The relevant comparison is performance across varied unfamiliar tasks, including failures, under comparable testing conditions.
criteria.support_condition: Broad, credible evaluations establish that contemporary systems lacked human-comparable flexibility, resourcefulness and reliability, with sufficient coverage to establish that claims of achieved general intelligence had no adequate empirical basis.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evaluations establish that a system existing by publication exhibited flexible, general capability with human-comparable resourcefulness and reliability across representative unfamiliar tasks. Success on one benchmark or an assertion using a weaker definition does not suffice.

evidence.explanation: The evaluator reports easy-task failures and cautions against equating benchmark success with AGI. This supports caution about an achievement claim, but the December test does not establish a universal absence of justification on the January target date.

This substantial result supplies evidence of adaptation to unfamiliar tasks, challenging a literal claim that there was no relevant evidence at all. One benchmark does not establish Marcus's broader requirement of human-comparable generality and reliability.

evidence.locator: Section 'Overview of the Joint Safety Research & Testing Exercise'
evidence.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
evidence.explanation: Pre-deployment testing identifies practical reliability problems, but the report expressly limits its findings to the tested version. The availability date conservatively uses the page's displayed update date; its original release was December 18, 2024.

The researchers publicly argued from cross-domain demonstrations that an early GPT-4 could be considered incomplete AGI. This is material counterevidence to the literal wording, but neither that interpretation nor these earlier demonstrations establish Marcus's reliability standard.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Broad, reproducible evaluations of systems existing by January 7, 2025, using representative unfamiliar tasks, matched human baselines, repeated trials and disclosed assistance, assessed against explicit standards for when flexibility, resourcefulness and reliability justify declaring general intelligence achieved.
